page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 8 dedicated physical cores based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 474 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results place the r8gd.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a PassMark CPU score of 7659.57 and a strong PassMark memory score of 2935.53, reflecting high memory efficiency. Read-only memory bandwidth reaches 925.12 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 169.31 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In database operations, the instance handles 11832.12 PassMark database operations and 16.62 million Redis SET operations per second.

While memory performance is strong, certain cryptographic and language model tasks show limitations. The PassMark CPU encryption test is rated as weak at 1507.08, and LLM inference for text generation on a medium 7B model is limited to 11.43 tokens per second. Given its high memory density, local NVMe storage, and solid database performance, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, caching layers, and database deployments that benefit from local scratch space.
